chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me; al-Mufaddal ibn Ziyad al-Abdi narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

We are a truthful household. Your main concern is the affairs of your religion, and the main concern of your enemies is you. Their hearts are filled with enmity against you; they distort everything they hear from you, consider others equal to you, and then accuse you of that out of slander. This is surely a sufficient act of disobedience in the sight of Allah.

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ: Ahl al-Bayt (the Household of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: How do the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt distort their words and what is the spiritual consequence?
ai.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to define the distinctive character of the Shia, emphasizing that the Ahl al-Bayt’s sincerity is often met with distortion by adversaries who, fueled by innate enmity, fabricate slanders. This narrative underscores the theological concept of *al-Bughd* (divine hatred) placed in the hearts of enemies, serving as a key marker of sectarian identity and spiritual resilience in Shia tradition. The Prophet’s declaration that this distortion is sufficient for their disobedience (*ma'siyyah*) validates the Ahl al-Bayt’s truthfulness despite external accusations.

en.badr-shahin: Mohammed bin Musa bin al-Mutawakkil, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated to me from Mohammed bin Yahya al-Attar from … al-Mufaddhal bin Ziyad al-Abdi that Abu Abdullah (a) said:

We are truthful household. Your main concern is the affairs of your religion. The main concern of your enemies is you. Their hearts are full of enmity against you. They distort the words that they hear from you, consider other things as equal to you, and they accuse you of such things out of slander. This is surely a sufficient act of disobedience in the sight of Allah.
